thread.title: 2 Analysts are Bearish on Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)!! Stock Downgraded “sector weight” & “market perform”

author: Douglas Bein
title: 2 Analysts are Bearish on Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)!! Stock Downgraded “sector weight” & “market perform”
text:
February 5, 2018 2 Analysts are Bearish on Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)!! Stock Downgraded “sector weight” & “market perform” 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) stock is facing headwinds, as in last week on Friday it traded lower, which is its lowest since late October, as on Friday, the broader market suffered its worst day in more than a year and Dow Jones index had its sixth largest point slump ever, and Apple was the fourth-worst performer in Dow. Following Thursday’s earnings report, the pace of Apple stocks was also determined on the basis of analysts, and two analyst firms have cut their ratings on AAPL stock after earnings report. 
Analyst at KeyBanc Capital Markets has downgraded Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) to “sector weight” from “overweight”. And an analyst at Bernstein has reduced AAPL stock to “market perform” from “outperform”. Both rating firms justified there ratings on Apple stock by pointed towards the slower demand of iPhone and make it a main reason behind their revision in AAPL ratings. 
Never the less, there are few more words on the company’s stock, among which the founder of the Bear Traps Report, Larry McDonald, sees a buying opportunity in Apple stock, but he thinks that this is surely a buy stock but not until the shares of Apple have suffered a little more. 
Larry McDonald anticipates the buy on the shares of Apple, by saying that 10 or so more trading days in the red for the company before he is actually ready to call it a “buy”. 
“The capitulation process is about 70 percent complete,” he said Friday on “Trading Nation.”“You’re going to get a spectacular opportunity to step in here and buy these fallen angels but you need a little bit more pain.” 
The head of sales and trading at Cowen, Dvaid Seaburg says about the company that it has not turned rotten, and he foresees this pullback presents an opportunity to “buy” Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) stock. 
“At these levels I think it’s kind of a no-brainer,” Seaburg told CNBC’s “Trading Nation” on Friday. 
“You’ve got this sort of cash on hand that they could do something with. If they flex their muscle and start to return cash to shareholders or make some sort of meaningful acquisition, that could be transformative,” said Seaburg. “The stock will be off to the races.” 
When on Thursday last week Apple posted its first quarter earnings, it’s a beat on its top and bottom lines for the first quarter, as it reported the slowing growth of in iPhone sales. 
The company said it sold 77.3 million smartphones in this quarter,that is down 1% on year over year basis. 
But still there are chances to pick up the growth as the company anticipates 13% to 17% sales growth in the line of iPhones with high priced, in the year 2018. About Douglas Bein
